Answer: B
Reason: The provided chest X-ray (Figure 3a) shows the azygos fissure as a distinct curvilinear line in the right upper lung field without the characteristic teardrop-shaped opacity of the azygos vein at its caudal end, indicating an "empty" fissure likely due to venous compression or displacement following pneumothorax and chest tube placement. This morphological finding aligns with option B, whereas the other options describe opacities or shifts not supported by the visible anatomy.
